trust_decision.summary: Whether a new release-attachment name set through the web release edit form passes the release extension allowlist (setting.Repository.Release.AllowedTypes). At the pinned commit this is already decided in release_service.UpdateRelease before the rename is stored.

landing_point.why: The summary names the web release edit form; the attachment-edit-<uuid> form keys are collected here and passed to UpdateRelease.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: the advisory's protection is already present at the pinned commit (services/release/release.go:327), so no solver task exists for it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Renaming a release attachment to another allowed name must keep working (test.txt -> test2.txt).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Attachments linked to a release by UUID (AddReleaseAttachments) are checked for repo ownership only, not against the release allowlist, so an issue-allowlisted upload could be linked to a release.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Issue and release uploads share one attachment table and one upload path (services/attachment/attachment.go:64-67 FIXME). A maintainer checking only the rename path would not think about linking.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The API attachment rename passes the release allowlist through UpdateAttachment. A copy that calls repo_model.UpdateAttachment directly would be the classic missed sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The web and API rename paths are separate implementations of the same rename in different packages.

O9_family: unrestricted file upload / extension allowlist bypass via rename (CWE-434, CWE-424)

O10_build.toolchain: go (version from go.mod), make; node/pnpm only for frontend assets
services: sqlite (embedded) for unit and integration tests
